newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco term naphtha offer at $6.50 premium - traders.
newsitem.headline: Aramco term naphtha offer at $6.50 premium - traders.

text.p: State-owned Saudi Aramco offered its A-180 term naphtha cargoes at about $6.50 above the Aramco formula for 1997, compared with the current $3.40 premium for the second half of 1996, traders here said on Thursday.
Aramco also suggested a $5.50 premium for Jubail and Rabigh naphtha, they added. In the current term, both Jubail and Rabigh are priced at $3.00 over the formula.
About a dozen potential naphtha buyers, most from Japan and South Korea, started the term naphtha talks with Aramco earlier this week in London.
Bidding levels from Japanese trading houses, which submitted their initial bids earlier this month, were around $4.50 over the formula, they said.

While some traders said Aramco's offer prices were too high to be accepted, others said new term prices are likely to be settled at around the offered levels as Aramco tends to negotiate on a take-it-or-leave-it basis.
"As a buyer, I'd hope there would be some room for negotiation, but I wonder how big it would be," one trader said.

In the previous term price negotiations for the second half of this year, Japanese and South Korean importers accepted Aramco's offer price of $3.40 over the formula for A-180, although they initially bid a premium of about $1.50 to $2.00.
The new term prices, expected to set a tone for term price talks with other naphtha exporters, will be set by the end of next week, traders said.
